songs.title: My Luva
songs.verdict: A smooth, unhurried love song that does its job as a warm-up for the EP, without yet showing much of who he is.
songs.body:
SleezeTeamJason is Shawn Jackson, an independent R&B singer from Hawthorne, California. “My Luva” is a short single, about two and a half minutes, meant to set up his My L.O.V.E. EP, due Nov 20.

**Melody & hook:** Remixd picked it from its submissions and framed it as a smooth love song, easygoing and easy to get into. **Vocals & delivery:** this is a singer's record, built for a relaxed, romantic mood. **Production** and **Lyrics:** no credits or detail are public yet, so judge them on the listen.

It's brief and low-pressure, which helps replays. The knock, going by the write-up: he's still shaping his own identity, and an agreeable love song in a crowded lane needs something distinctive to stick.
songs.scout_note: Remixd Magazine 'From Our Submissions' pick, New Music Friday Nov 6 (remixdmagazine.com/new-music-friday-week-of-november-6/). Small independent artist; listener count not checked.

songs.title: Disturbia (feat. Thuqga Lucifer)
songs.verdict: Miami Gardens emo rap with a gothic-rock shadow, pitched as a spiritual battle. The mood is set; the payoff still has to be proven.
songs.body:
XRITUAL is a Miami Gardens artist working where emo rap meets gothic rock, and "Disturbia" (out Nov 1, with Thuqga Lucifer on the feature) is the kind of dark, melodic cut that lane runs on. He frames the record as a spiritual battle and has been pushing it through The Reckoning Artist Showcase in South Florida.

**Melody & hook:** press describes it as melodic first, darkness second. **Vocals & delivery:** a two-voice track, with the feature there to add weight. **Production:** the gothic-rock tint is the selling point over standard emo-trap beats.

One roundup mention is all the coverage so far, so the score holds in the middle until the listen. The local angle is real; whether it stands out in a crowded lane is the open question.
songs.scout_note: South Florida artist (local angle for @wackometer and the QR stickers). Remixd Magazine 'In Case You Missed It', Nov 6 roundup. Spotify link is the single's release page.

songs.title: BURNT PAGES
songs.verdict: A ten-track Queens rap album built around loss and perseverance, with a guest list that shows where STORY stands in the city's scene.
songs.body:
STORY is a Queens rapper, and BURNT PAGES (out Oct 28, a day after a Brooklyn release event) is a ten-track album that uses fire and burned-paper imagery to frame songs about loss and pushing through.

**Lyrics:** loss and perseverance are the stated core, which puts the weight on the writing. **Features:** Dusty Locane, Millyz, Kocky Ka, Top Gee, Cosi Pari and BigBaby Juss give it a deep bench of East Coast guests. **Production:** no credits surfaced, so the beats are the critic's call. Standout track: none named in coverage yet; pick one after listening.

The knock for now is visibility: one roundup mention and a Spotify embed is all the press it has. The guest list says people in the scene take him seriously; whether the album holds ten tracks on its own is what a listen has to settle.
songs.scout_note: Released Oct 28. Remixd Magazine 'In Case You Missed It', Nov 6 roundup. Album: pick a standout track in the review.

songs.title: Make them Wonder
songs.verdict: Afrobeats bounce, bright pop polish and a warm, playful vocal on a single built to get a room moving.
songs.body:
OWO grew up between Nigeria and Prince George’s County, Maryland, has opened for Burna Boy and Wizkid, and debuted with the SEEDs EP in 2021. “Make them Wonder” is her October single and a teaser for a bigger project: a confident, self-assured cut blending R&B, Afropop, pop and dance.

**Melody & hook:** press hears a lively rhythm made for the stage rather than a slow burn. **Vocals & delivery:** smooth and warm, with a confident, playful edge. **Production** comes from Tobby Badass, with Matt Cody mixing and mastering, pairing Afrobeats textures with bright pop sheen. **Lyrics:** a self-belief song that turns into a cheeky claim that nobody can copy her, tied to the Nigerian idea of “gbas gbos,” energies colliding.

Replay depends on how much you want an upbeat confidence anthem in rotation. The knock: self-expression anthems are a crowded shelf, and the coverage so far is roundup-level, so this still has to prove it stands apart.
songs.scout_note: Released Oct 16. Remixd Magazine 'In Case You Missed It', Nov 6 roundup. Spotify link is the single's release page.

songs.title: Limbo¿
songs.verdict: Pumping bass, jazzy keys and a vocal that slips between singing and rapping: messy on purpose, and more alive for it.
songs.body:
i.B. Dollface is a Canadian singer working between electro-pop and alternative R&B. “Limbo¿” (3:13) never settles into one genre, and that restlessness is the point.

**Production** carries it: pumping bass and upbeat drums drive it, while a soulful piano-synth line with jazz touches adds warmth. **Vocals & delivery:** she moves between singing and rap-shaped phrasing in a sultry, volatile way that Uranium Waves compares to early-2000s crossover R&B. **Melody & hook:** the appeal comes from contrast more than from one big chorus.

The groove makes it easy to run back. The honest limit, per the same write-up, is that the vocal sometimes sits slightly outside the groove; that friction gives it character, but it reads as less polished.
songs.scout_note: Covered by Uranium Waves (Canadian discovery blog), Nov 8. Release date not stated; covered this week. Small artist. NOTE: Spotify says Feb 2026, older than the 60-day window.

songs.title: Entropy
songs.verdict: A Guelph soul collective turns a decade of chronic illness into alt R&B that grooves while it aches.
songs.body:
SHEBAD is a Guelph, Ontario band built around bassist Mark Spagnolo and singer Claire Voy, pulling soul, jazz, fusion and funk into alternative R&B. "Entropy" draws on Voy's decade living with endometriosis: a body wearing down while the work week carries on, with a brief daydream of floating somewhere painless before reality returns.

**Melody & hook:** syncopated, glassy guitar riffs over a heavy, soulful bassline and upbeat live drums. **Vocals & delivery:** Voy's tone is described as velvety and yearning, backed by layered harmonies. **Production** is clean and uncluttered. **Lyrics:** the strength here, refusing to paint illness as pure tragedy or triumph.

The subject gives it weight most groove records don't have. The knock to check on the listen: a busy fusion band can blur a song's center, so the hook needs to cut through the playing.
songs.scout_note: Uranium Waves feature, Nov 3. Small independent band.

songs.title: Here I Am
songs.verdict: A ninth solo album of off-center Canadian rap where the dark, sparse beats do more than the steady flow.
songs.body:
Ezza of Choom Gang is a Canadian rapper with a long self-directed run, and Here I Am is his ninth solo album: 13 tracks on struggle, ambition and self-discovery, pulling from Southern rap, East Coast boom bap and darker atmospheric rap.

**Production:** the most interesting part. Opener “Lake America” is built on haunting samples and subdued synths with almost no drums, and “Serotonin Syndrome” goes darkest. **Lyrics:** eccentric and narrative, with “What's Grief?” as the inward one. **Vocals & delivery:** relaxed and steady, maybe too steady; the cadence rarely shifts. Standout: “Wear My Heart” with AYOO BIGZ and BOOGIE MASON, the most classic boom bap cut, soulful and drum-heavy.

Replay comes from the mood more than hooks. The honest limit, echoed by Uranium Waves: songs could use more structure and melodic lift, and the jump into the bass-heavy closer “Down Good” with Wingman777 feels abrupt. Not for anyone after polished radio rap.
songs.scout_note: Uranium Waves album review, Nov 4. Underground, self-directed. Album: pick a standout track in the review.

songs.title: Machine
songs.verdict: colby! trades alt-pop sweetness for an M.I.A.-tinted punk sneer, aimed squarely at the people who doubted her.
songs.body:
colby! is a Texas-raised alt-pop artist in her early twenties who writes with her older brother RJ Johnson and has been flagged as one to watch by Fault and Galore. “Machine” is her move toward the punk sound she’s been circling, with M.I.A. as the stated reference point.

**Production:** it starts on acoustic guitar and builds into something gritty and drum-heavy, with layered synths and driven guitars. **Vocals & delivery:** reviewers call her controlled and emotive, composed even when the words get sharp. **Lyrics:** a self-described passive-aggressive empowerment song about people who belittled her young and now want back in once she’s winning. **Melody & hook:** the energy is groove-first, with the attitude doing most of the work.

It suits a playlist that wants bite without full punk abrasion. The limit: the comeback-at-the-doubters theme is well worn, and how fresh it feels will rest on whether the punk turn sounds lived-in or like a costume.
songs.scout_note: Uranium Waves feature, Nov 8. Small artist. CHECK SIZE: Rock the Pigeon (Nov 7) says 550K+ monthly listeners.

songs.title: Running Away
songs.verdict: Matilde G turns walking away from a love triangle into a fired-up rock anthem with a chorus that sticks.
songs.body:
Matilde G is an Italian pop singer who has moved through several sounds, and “Running Away” (2:23, from the album Beautiful Wreckage) is her edgier, rock-leaning turn. It's about unwanted attention, temptation and getting out of a love triangle with your self-respect intact.

**Melody & hook:** Ratings Game Music singles out a catchy chorus and an infectious melody. **Vocals & delivery:** spirited and passionate, keeping the attitude up. **Production:** hard-hitting drums and driving rock elements. **Lyrics:** the strength is making the exit sound assertive, not sad.

At under two and a half minutes it's built to replay. The knock: reception so far is warm but measured (RGM gave it 3.5/5), and the edgy-pop-rock lane is crowded, so it has to win on the chorus.
songs.scout_note: Uranium Waves feature, Nov 8. Small artist. NOTE: released Oct 2025 per Spotify, older than the 60-day window.

songs.title: Sucker Punch
songs.verdict: Worn-in indie folk-pop about leaving someone who hurt you, building tension by circling rather than exploding.
songs.body:
Kaitlyn Fox is a Nashville-based singer-songwriter (and author of a music-business book) making indie folk-pop with a lo-fi edge. "Sucker Punch" is about trying to get out of a relationship where both people are wounded, and finding that the road out keeps pointing back. In her own framing, it's about wounds that stay open after you've walked away.

**Melody & hook:** no big folk crescendo; tension builds through repetition and texture. **Vocals & delivery:** a yearning, slightly rough voice sits up front in the mix. **Production:** gentle guitars over lo-fi percussion, deliberately weathered rather than polished. **Lyrics:** physical, rural imagery, roads, power lines, bruises and wreckage.

It's a mood piece that rewards close listening. The limit: a song that refuses to break open can also feel like it never arrives.
songs.scout_note: Uranium Waves feature, Nov 2. Small artist.

songs.title: withforwardmotion
songs.verdict: Grungegaze with real weight: thick fuzz, hazy melodies and hardcore breakdowns, three years in the making.
songs.body:
Day Aches come out of the D.C./Virginia scene, and withforwardmotion, their second album and first for Other People Records, took about three years. It pushes their grunge-leaning shoegaze toward hardcore and nü metal, in the company of Narrow Head, Superheaven and Soul Blind.

**Production:** thick distorted guitars and reverb haze, cut with hard breakdowns. **Singles:** “In Water” is about reclaiming self-worth after heartbreak and abuse and drops into one of the record's heaviest breakdowns; “outerheaven” wears an early-2000s nü metal sheen. **Lyrics:** identity, uncertainty and time passing. Standouts per coverage lean dreamier: “Rei III”, “Exit Wounds”, “Re-Take After” and the title track.

Ten songs is a tight run, and switching between heavy and dreamy gives it shape. The knock: this lane is crowded right now, and the comparisons come easy; whether Day Aches sound like themselves rather than their peers is what to listen for.
songs.scout_note: Released Nov 4 (Release Wave November list). Links are to the artist pages; no album-specific link found, so the desk has no built-in player. Open Bandcamp to listen.

songs.title: Where Could I Go?
songs.verdict: Hook-first Atlanta punk about loving people through grief, work and failure, from a band that knows its lane cold.
songs.body:
New Junk City have been at it in Atlanta since 2013, and Where Could I Go? is their fourth full-length, out on Lauren Records. They’ve joked that they sound like Tom Petty played by Green Day, and the touchstones press cites run from The Weakerthans to The Menzingers and Japandroids. Twelve songs, written over about two years.

**Lyrics:** the record is about building a life around love: holding space for someone else’s grief, the compromises work demands, and owning your failures without turning bitter. Lead single “Lonely Now” is about drawing a line after repeated letdowns instead of hitting back; “Shell Game” asks how much of yourself to trade for stability. **Production:** recorded at Standard Electric with longtime collaborator Damon Moon and produced by Tyler Bisson. **Melody & hook:** the pitch is melodic, hook-driven urgency.

If heart-on-sleeve pop punk is your thing, there’s a lot to come back to. The knock: the reference points are familiar, and nothing documented yet suggests the band pushes past its well-loved template.
songs.scout_note: Released Nov 6 (Release Wave November list). Artist-page links only. Check they're under the underground cutoff before publishing.

songs.title: A Portrait of Fear
songs.verdict: A reverb-soaked third LP that pairs heavy grunge guitars with shoegaze swirl, wearing its 90s influences in plain view.
songs.body:
Melodic Canvas is the project of Northern Michigan musician and visual artist Evan Alderton, around since 2016. A Portrait of Fear is his third LP, ten tracks out Nov 4 on Setterwind and Candlepin Records, following Sterile (2021) and Discoloration (2024).

**Production** is the draw: the release notes describe haunting, reverb-heavy alt rock where grunge guitars meet shoegaze swirl, with eerie atmospheres. **Melody & hook:** the same notes stress melodic urgency, and the 2026 singles (Limn, Shacket, Dust) hint at the tighter songs. **Vocals & Lyrics:** fear and 90s alt angst set the mood; check the specifics on the listen.

The named touchstones (Nirvana, Smashing Pumpkins, Hum, Superheaven) say a lot about who this is for. The knock: wearing influences that openly can make a record feel like a tribute, and ten tracks of heavy reverb risks sameness.
songs.scout_note: Released Nov 4 on Setterwind / Candlepin Records (Release Wave). Artist-page links only.

songs.title: High Horse
songs.verdict: A self-produced debut of short, fuzzy, hook-first pop-punk that sounds like a bedroom project that grew teeth.
songs.body:
FFO: Chillin started in 2023 as a DIY bedroom project in Concord, New Hampshire and grew into a band that's opened for Joyce Manor and Glitterer. High Horse, their self-produced debut on DAZE (a label better known for heavy hardcore), arrived Nov 6, and Stereogum called their sound a supremely fun strain of alt-leaning pop-punk with occasional breakdowns.

**Melody & hook:** loud, hooky and fuzzy, built on punchy riffs and shout-along choruses. **Vocals & delivery:** single "Fresh Start" (about 85 seconds) borrows an emo-rap delivery that works better than you'd expect. **Lyrics:** cynicism with a grin, the shrug of having seen it coming. **Production** stays DIY.

The songs are very short, which keeps it moving and replayable. The knock: short and chaotic can blur together across a full album, and that's what the listen needs to settle.
songs.scout_note: Released Nov 6 (Release Wave November list). Debut album, small band.

songs.title: Vacas Flacas
songs.verdict: A Medellín songwriter steps out solo, mixing street rap with salsa and Caribbean rhythm.
songs.body:
Kapla is from Medellín and was half of Kapla y Miky, a duo whose members wrote for Maluma, Karol G and Feid before recording their own reggaeton. “Vacas Flacas” (Spotify lists it as an Oct 9 single) is part of his new solo run, with about 2.9K monthly listeners on his own profile.

**Production:** Remixd Magazine describes Latin hip-hop with a salsa influence, street rap set against Caribbean rhythm. **Lyrics:** the title is Colombian slang for lean, broke times, so expect hustle themes, but no write-up covers the words; check after listening. **Vocals & delivery:** not described; his songwriting background is the thing to test against the hook.

Remixd called it a solid find from its submissions, and that is the extent of the coverage. The knock: salsa-rap blends are not new, so it has to win on writing and groove.
songs.scout_note: Remixd Magazine 'From Our Submissions', Nov 6 roundup. Heads up: the old duo may have had a big following, so check his listener count; if he's over the cutoff, tick Big One or skip.
